IncidentBot: ALERT: node node-gpu-23 ephemeral storage > 95% (kubelet eviction pressure). Recent evictions: modelcache-*, serve-runtime-* pods. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Alex (oncall): acked. I'm on it, going to gather which pods evicted and customer impact.
Ryan (sre): seeing repeat Evicted reason 'ephemeral-storage'. Also kernel logs show writeback stalls.
Lee (infra): I can access node, running df -h and du to find large dirs.
Carla (runtime): modelcache pods showing repeated restarts. Some instances failing with CUDA init errors after restart, suspect corrupted checkpoint files plus low tmpfs.
Alex (oncall): what's the customer impact? Any 5xx spike?
Ryan (sre): yes, elevated 503 and increased latency ~500-1200ms for model-heavy routes. Affected tenants: a few enterprise customers on dedicated pool.
Alex (oncall): priority = P0. We need live mitigation: prevent further evictions and restore modelcache capacity.
Lee (infra): quick triage: /var/lib/modelcache and /var/log/journal are largest. journal size ~42G (tmpfs used for journald?). looks like logrotate didn't purge.
Carla (runtime): modelcache writes heavy logs on failed loads, cycles. If journal keeps growing it eats tmpfs -> kube evicts pods.
Alex (oncall): immediate plan: 1) stop noisy pods on node, 2) rotate/truncate journal, 3) cordon node, 4) drain safe pods, 5) restart modelcache with cleared checkpoints where necessary. Can we do that quickly?
Lee (infra): starting with truncated journal: 

```bash
ssh root@node-gpu-23
# show big files
du -sh /var/log/journal/* | sort -h
# truncate current journal (atomic)
journalctl --vacuum-size=200M || true
# if journalctl blocked, fallback
cp /dev/null /var/log/journal/*/system.journal || true
systemctl restart systemd-journald || true
```

Lee (infra): ran vacuum-size=200M; freed ~40GB. journald restarted.
Alex (oncall): great. Next: cordon node and evict remaining non-critical pods.
Lee (infra): cordoned node-gpu-23. Starting drain for non-dedicated pods: 

```bash
kubectl cordon node-gpu-23
kubectl drain node-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

Lee (infra): drain completed for bench, dev pods. Dedicated modelcache and serve-runtime pods were evicted/terminated as expected and rescheduled elsewhere.
Carla (runtime): restarted two modelcache replicas on other nodes, but one retry fails during model load with CUDA OOM despite GPU available. Logs: 

```
E runtime: failed to init CUDA context: cuInit failed, error 700
E modelcache: Model load failed: not enough device memory, attempted 24GB, available 8GB
```

Carla (runtime): looks like kernel still holding memory refs or driver flaked after repeated crashes. I recommend restarting nvidia-driver pod on target node and re-scheduling workload.
Lee (infra): restarted gpu-driver-host service on node-gpu-19 where reschedule landed. Cleared GPU memory.
Alex (oncall): any persistent corrupted checkpoints we should remove?
Carla (runtime): found a 6GB temp checkpoint under /var/lib/modelcache/tmp/checkpoint.tmp on node-gpu-23. I moved it to /tmp to avoid auto-load and freed space. We'll rehydrate from S3 after stabilization.
Ryan (sre): monitoring shows eviction events stopped after cordon+journal cleanup. Disk usage normalized to <60% on node-gpu-23.
Alex (oncall): customer impact update: we saw degraded latency and 5xxs for ~12 minutes for limited set of customers on dedicated pool; failover to other nodes completed for most traffic. I'll draft a short customer note.
Alex (oncall): next steps (short):
- uncordon node only after verifying docker/nvidia driver stable (Carla + Lee)
- re-enable auto-scheduling gradually, watch for restart loops
- add journald vacuum policy to infra runbook and alert thresholds for /var/log/journal growth
- add runtime guard to throttle logging during repeated model load failures

Carla (runtime): opened PR for runtime log throttling and to avoid writing verbose stack traces to journal in a tight loop. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/3212
Ryan (sre): setting an alert rule: node ephem_percent > 85% for 10m to page infra team earlier.
Lee (infra): follow-up cleanup commands I ran: 

```bash
# removed stale tmp checkpoints
rm -rf /var/lib/modelcache/tmp/*
# validate journal vacuum schedule
cat /etc/systemd/journald.conf | grep -E "^SystemMaxUse|^RuntimeMaxUse" || true
```

DeployBot: Deploy succeeded: runtime logging throttling v1.0 rolled to canary (2/20) at 1746000300.
Alex (oncall): handing off to Ryan for next 8h oncall monitoring and post-incident writeup. I'll add initial timeline and impact summary.
Ryan (sre): taking over. I'll keep watches on eviction events, GPU failures, and customer error rate.
Alex (oncall): thanks team. final notes: duration ~00:24, impact: limited customers experienced degraded service and transient 5xxs while modelcache pods were evicted; root cause: runaway journald/log growth in tmpfs combined with model load crash loop writing logs -> ephemeral storage exhaustion -> kubelet eviction cascade.
Carla (runtime): will follow up with regression test to ensure modelcache doesn't log verbosely on repeated failures.
Ryan (sre): creating postmortem draft and linking to incident board.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) at 1746000450.
